lesson_title: Three Shortcuts and Two Special Numbers
hook_text: 4 times 7 times 25 in your head? Easy, if you change the grouping.
clip_script: Prize-giving in Kimberley. 4 times 7 times 25. Left to right is hard. So group differently: 4 times 25 is 100. 100 times 7 is 700. Done. Next, 37 plus 48 plus 63. Pair 37 with 63 to make 100. Plus 48 is 148. Now 23 tickets at R25. Split 23 into 20 and 3. 20 times 25 is 500. 3 times 25 is 75. R575. But careful: never swap or regroup minus and divide. 50 minus 20 is 30, and 20 minus 50 is not. Last, two special numbers. Plus 0 changes nothing. Times 1 changes nothing. Swap, group, split, and know your 0 and 1.
visual_style: Rows of chairs turning sideways, number cards pairing up into 100s, and a ticket roll splitting into 20 and 3.
mood: Clever and quick, like a magician revealing a trick.
pacing: Three fast shortcuts, a warning beat, then the two special numbers.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the friendliest pair in 25 plus 39 plus 75.
